name: ATF_TC_BODY(int8, tc)
prose: ATF test body (function int8_body). It runs one non-fatal check, ATF_CHECK(INT8_MIN < UINT8_MAX), which compares the constants -128 and 255 and passes in normal C integer arithmetic. It reads no state and changes nothing; a failed check would only be recorded and the test would continue.

name: ATF_TC_BODY(int16, tc)
prose: ATF test body (function int16_body). It runs one non-fatal check, ATF_CHECK(INT16_MIN < UINT16_MAX), comparing the constants -32768 and 65535; it passes in normal C integer arithmetic. No state is read or changed.

name: ATF_TC_BODY(check_sdp_put_str, tc)
prose: ATF test body (function check_sdp_put_str_body) for sdp_put_str. It sets up a 512-byte buffer and an sdp_data_t (next at the start, end at the end), then with ATF_REQUIRE (fatal on failure) puts four strings: "Hello World!" with length 5, "Hello\0World" with length 11, "Hello World!" with length -1 and "Hello\0World" with length -1 (the last two use the C string length). It then sets end = next and next = buf and requires the encoded length to equal the expected array (str8 headers 0x25 with lengths 5, 11, 12 and 5 followed by the data bytes); finally it compares the bytes with ATF_CHECK(memcmp(...) == 0), which is non-fatal, so a byte mismatch is recorded but the test continues; a length mismatch is fatal.
note: contrib/netbsd-tests/lib/libbluetooth/t_sdp_put.c:771-805. Reviewer (r15) RIGHT: the memcmp ATF_CHECK is non-fatal (:804).

name: ATF_TC_BODY(check_sdp_put_url, tc)
prose: ATF test body (function check_sdp_put_url_body) for sdp_put_url. With a 512-byte buffer and an sdp_data_t over it it requires (fatal) that sdp_put_url succeeds for "http://www.netbsd.org/" with length 21 (dropping the trailing slash) and with length -1 (the whole string). It then sets end = next and next = buf, requires the encoded size to equal the expected array (url8 header 0x45 with lengths 0x15 and 0x16 plus the characters), and compares the bytes with ATF_CHECK(memcmp(...) == 0), which only records a failure.
note: contrib/netbsd-tests/lib/libbluetooth/t_sdp_put.c:815-847. Reviewer (r15) RIGHT: memcmp ATF_CHECK is non-fatal (:846).

name: ATF_TC_BODY(libbpfjit_ldx_imm1, tc)
prose: Each of these ATF bodies builds a static BPF program, checks it with bpf_validate (ATF_CHECK, non-fatal), compiles it with bpfjit_generate_code (ATF_REQUIRE that the result is not NULL), runs it through the jitcall helper (which fills a bpf_args_t with the packet, wirelen and buflen and calls the compiled function with a NULL context) and frees the code with bpfjit_free_code. Program: X = UINT32_MAX - 5 (BPF_LDX+BPF_W+BPF_IMM), A += X, return A. Since A starts at 0 the check is jitcall(code, pkt, 1, 1) == UINT32_MAX - 5; the one-byte packet is not read.

name: ATF_TC_BODY(libbpfjit_ldx_imm2, tc)
prose: Each of these ATF bodies builds a static BPF program, checks it with bpf_validate (ATF_CHECK, non-fatal), compiles it with bpfjit_generate_code (ATF_REQUIRE that the result is not NULL), runs it through the jitcall helper (which fills a bpf_args_t with the packet, wirelen and buflen and calls the compiled function with a NULL context) and frees the code with bpfjit_free_code. Program: X = 5, A = 5, if A == X skip the next instruction, return 7, return UINT32_MAX. The check is jitcall(code, pkt, 1, 1) == UINT32_MAX (the equal case skips the 'return 7').

name: ATF_TC_BODY(libbpfjit_ldx_len1, tc)
prose: Each of these ATF bodies builds a static BPF program, checks it with bpf_validate (ATF_CHECK, non-fatal), compiles it with bpfjit_generate_code (ATF_REQUIRE that the result is not NULL), runs it through the jitcall helper (which fills a bpf_args_t with the packet, wirelen and buflen and calls the compiled function with a NULL context) and frees the code with bpfjit_free_code. Program: X = packet length (BPF_LEN), A += X, return A. For i = 1..4 it checks jitcall(code, pkt, i, 1) == i and jitcall(code, pkt, i + 1, i) == i + 1, i.e. the result equals the wirelen argument, independent of buflen; the packet bytes are not read.

name: ATF_TC_BODY(libbpfjit_ldx_len2, tc)
prose: Each of these ATF bodies builds a static BPF program, checks it with bpf_validate (ATF_CHECK, non-fatal), compiles it with bpfjit_generate_code (ATF_REQUIRE that the result is not NULL), runs it through the jitcall helper (which fills a bpf_args_t with the packet, wirelen and buflen and calls the compiled function with a NULL context) and frees the code with bpfjit_free_code. Program: X = packet length, A = 5, if A == X skip the next instruction, return 7, return UINT32_MAX. Checks jitcall(code, pkt, 5, 1) == UINT32_MAX (wirelen 5 equals A) and jitcall(code, pkt, 6, 5) == 7 (wirelen 6 differs).

name: ATF_TC_BODY(libbpfjit_ldx_msh, tc)
prose: Each of these ATF bodies builds a static BPF program, checks it with bpf_validate (ATF_CHECK, non-fatal), compiles it with bpfjit_generate_code (ATF_REQUIRE that the result is not NULL), runs it through the jitcall helper (which fills a bpf_args_t with the packet, wirelen and buflen and calls the compiled function with a NULL context) and frees the code with bpfjit_free_code. Program: X = 4 * (pkt[1] & 0xf) (BPF_LDX+BPF_B+BPF_MSH with offset 1), A += X, return A. With pkt = {0, 0x7a} the check is jitcall(code, pkt, 2, 2) == 40 (0x7a & 0xf = 10, times 4).

name: ATF_TC_BODY(libbpfjit_misc_tax, tc)
prose: Each of these ATF bodies builds a static BPF program, checks it with bpf_validate (ATF_CHECK, non-fatal), compiles it with bpfjit_generate_code (ATF_REQUIRE that the result is not NULL), runs it through the jitcall helper (which fills a bpf_args_t with the packet, wirelen and buflen and calls the compiled function with a NULL context) and frees the code with bpfjit_free_code. Program: A = 3, X = A (BPF_MISC+BPF_TAX), A = byte at pkt[X + 2], return A. With pkt = {0, 11, 22, 33, 44, 55} the check is jitcall(code, pkt, 6, 6) == 55 (pkt[5]).

name: ATF_TC_BODY(libbpfjit_misc_txa, tc)
prose: Each of these ATF bodies builds a static BPF program, checks it with bpf_validate (ATF_CHECK, non-fatal), compiles it with bpfjit_generate_code (ATF_REQUIRE that the result is not NULL), runs it through the jitcall helper (which fills a bpf_args_t with the packet, wirelen and buflen and calls the compiled function with a NULL context) and frees the code with bpfjit_free_code. Program: X = 391, A = X (BPF_MISC+BPF_TXA), return A. The check is jitcall(code, pkt, 1, 1) == 391; the one-byte packet is not read.

name: ATF_TC_BODY(libbpfjit_st1, tc)
prose: Each of these ATF bodies builds a static BPF program, checks it with bpf_validate (ATF_CHECK, non-fatal), compiles it with bpfjit_generate_code (ATF_REQUIRE that the result is not NULL), runs it through the jitcall helper (which fills a bpf_args_t with the packet, wirelen and buflen and calls the compiled function with a NULL context) and frees the code with bpfjit_free_code. Program: A = packet length, store A in scratch M[0] (BPF_ST), A += 1, A = M[0] (BPF_LD+BPF_MEM), return A. For i = 1..16 with a 16-byte packet it checks jitcall(code, pkt, i, 16) == i, i.e. the stored length is returned, not length + 1.

name: ATF_TC_BODY(fexecve, tc)
prose: ATF test body for fexecve (function ATF_TC_BODY_fexecve). It forks (ATF_REQUIRE). The child opens /usr/bin/touch read-only (exiting with EXIT_FAILURE through err() if that fails) and calls fexecve(fd, {"touch","test"}, empty environment); if fexecve returns -1 the child closes fd and exits with status 76 when errno is ENOSYS, otherwise EXIT_FAILURE. The parent waits (ATF_REQUIRE the wait succeeds), fails the test if the child did not exit normally, and if the status is 76 calls atf_tc_expect_fail("fexecve not implemented"); otherwise it requires the exit status to be EXIT_SUCCESS. In all non-failed paths it then requires access("test", F_OK) == 0, i.e. that the touched file "test" exists in the current directory. With status 76 that last requirement is normally expected to fail, but if a file named "test" already exists it passes and the expected failure becomes an unexpected pass. The test also depends on /usr/bin/touch being executable and openable.
note: contrib/netbsd-tests/lib/libc/c063/t_fexecve.c:53-87. Reviewer (r15) RIGHT: executable permission is an implicit precondition and an existing 'test' file turns the status-76 case into an unexpected pass.

name: ATF_TC_BODY(floatunditf, tc)
prose: ATF test body checking uint64 to long double conversion. Without __HAVE_LONG_DOUBLE it calls atf_tc_skip and the loop is not built. On FreeBSD/i386 it first declares an expected failure (atf_tc_expect_fail). Otherwise, for each of the table's entries (a 64-bit unsigned value and the exactly expected long double) it uses ATF_CHECK_MSG (non-fatal) that (long double)u64 == the expected value, printing the index and both values with %.20Lf on mismatch. It returns nothing.

name: ATF_TC_BODY(fpsetmask_basic, tc)
prose: ATF test body for fpsetmask/fpgetmask. After FPU_PREREQ() it reads the current mask msk = fpgetmask(). For each of FP_X_INV, FP_X_DZ, FP_X_OFL and FP_X_UFL it sets the mask to msk | bit and checks with ATF_CHECK (non-fatal) that fpgetmask() has the bit set, then sets the mask to msk & ~bit and checks the bit is clear. The last step leaves the mask as msk & ~FP_X_UFL, so the original mask is not restored (an FP_X_UFL bit that was set originally ends up cleared). Failed checks are recorded and the test continues.
note: contrib/netbsd-tests/lib/libc/gen/t_fpsetmask.c:336-351. Reviewer (r15) RIGHT: ATF_CHECK does not abort. Not read: FPU_PREREQ.

name: ATF_TC_BODY(sethostname_basic, tc)
prose: ATF test body for sethostname/gethostname; its first statement is atf_tc_skip("screws up the test host's hostname on FreeBSD"), which ends the test as skipped, so the rest is not reached in this file. The code after it would, for each of four hostnames in the hosts table (MAXHOSTNAMELEN-sized arrays), clear a name buffer, set the hostname (on FreeBSD with length sizeof - 1 after size sanity checks, elsewhere with the full array size), read it back with gethostname and require equality with strcmp, and finally restore the saved hostname. The test requires root.

name: ATF_TC_CLEANUP(sethostname_basic, tc)
prose: ATF cleanup routine: restores the hostname saved at test-program start by calling sethostname(host, sizeof(host)); the result is cast away and ignored. `host` is the static buffer filled by gethostname when the tests are registered.

name: ATF_TC_BODY(sethostname_limit, tc)
prose: ATF test body checking that a too long hostname is rejected. It zero-fills a buffer of MAXHOSTNAMELEN + 1 bytes and requires (fatal) that sethostname(name, sizeof(name)) returns -1. Runs as root (require.user = root).

name: ATF_TC_CLEANUP(sethostname_limit, tc)
prose: ATF cleanup routine. On FreeBSD it first requires (ATF_REQUIRE) that sethostname(host, MAXHOSTNAMELEN - 1) returns 0 and sethostname(host, MAXHOSTNAMELEN) returns -1; on every platform it then restores the saved hostname with sethostname(host, sizeof(host)), ignoring that result. So on FreeBSD the cleanup can itself fail a requirement.

name: ATF_TC_BODY(sethostname_perm, tc)
prose: ATF test body checking that an unprivileged user cannot set the hostname (require.user = unprivileged). It sets errno = 0 and requires (ATF_REQUIRE_ERRNO) that sethostname(host, sizeof(host)) returns -1 with errno EPERM.

name: ATF_TC_CLEANUP(sethostname_perm, tc)
prose: ATF cleanup routine: calls sethostname(host, sizeof(host)) to restore the saved hostname and ignores the result.

name: ATF_TC_BODY(mbrtowc_internal, tc)
prose: ATF test body that runs h_ctype2(t, false) for each entry of the tests table (C, en_US.UTF-8, ja_JP.ISO2022-JP2, ja_JP.SJIS, ja_JP.eucJP) until an entry with data == NULL. h_ctype2 sets the locale (fatal on NetBSD if missing; on other systems it prints 'Locale not found' and returns, skipping that entry), then for chunk sizes n = 9 down to 1 decodes the entry's data with mbrtowc using the internal state (stp = NULL), requires an initial state, checks each wide character and byte width against the table (atf_tc_fail on mismatch or an invalid sequence), requires the terminating character 0 and the expected length, and finally checks mbsrtowcs over the whole string. Returns nothing.

name: ATF_TC_BODY(mbrtowc_object, tc)
prose: ATF test body identical to mbrtowc_internal except that it calls h_ctype2(t, true), so the mbrtowc and mbsrtowcs calls use an explicit, zero-initialised mbstate_t object instead of the internal state; it iterates over every table entry until data == NULL and fails through the helper's checks.

name: ATF_TC_BODY(wctomb, tc)
prose: ATF test body that runs h_wctomb(t, TC_WCTOMB) for each entry of the tests table until data == NULL. h_wctomb sets the locale (fatal on NetBSD if missing; on other systems it prints 'Locale not found' and returns without testing that entry), converts the entry's data to wide characters with mbsrtowcs (requiring the expected count and a terminating 0), and then for each of the wclen + 1 characters calls wctomb(cs, wcs[i]) and compares the returned byte count with the expected mblen[i], calling atf_tc_fail at the first mismatch. It first prints a heading.
note: contrib/netbsd-tests/lib/libc/locale/t_wctomb.c:163-171 calling h_wctomb :100-156. Reviewer (r15) RIGHT: the locale-not-found early return on non-NetBSD systems is part of the helper (:115-118).

name: ATF_TC_BODY(wcrtomb_state, tc)
prose: ATF test body that runs h_wctomb(t, TC_WCRTOMB_ST) for each entry of the tests table until data == NULL. h_wctomb sets the locale (fatal on NetBSD if missing; on other systems it prints 'Locale not found' and returns without testing that entry), converts the entry's data to wide characters with mbsrtowcs (requiring the expected count and a terminating 0), and then for each of the wclen + 1 characters calls wcrtomb(cs, wcs[i], &st) with a zero-initialised mbstate_t object and compares the returned byte count with the expected mblen[i], calling atf_tc_fail at the first mismatch. It first prints a heading.
note: contrib/netbsd-tests/lib/libc/locale/t_wctomb.c:179-187 calling h_wctomb :100-156 (state object set up at :127-130).

name: ATF_TC_BODY(wcrtomb, tc)
prose: ATF test body that runs h_wctomb(t, TC_WCRTOMB) for each entry of the tests table until data == NULL. h_wctomb sets the locale (fatal on NetBSD if missing; on other systems it prints 'Locale not found' and returns without testing that entry), converts the entry's data to wide characters with mbsrtowcs (requiring the expected count and a terminating 0), and then for each of the wclen + 1 characters calls wcrtomb(cs, wcs[i], NULL), i.e. with the internal state and compares the returned byte count with the expected mblen[i], calling atf_tc_fail at the first mismatch. It first prints a heading.

name: efind
prose: Static helper in the regex test driver: converts a regerror error name (the part after "REG_") to its numeric code. It formats "REG_<name>" into a static 100-byte buffer with sprintf (the length assertion comes after the write, so an over-long name overflows before it is checked), sets re.re_endp to that buffer, calls regerror(REG_ATOI, &re, efbuf, sizeof(efbuf)), which writes the decimal code of the named error into efbuf, and returns atoi(efbuf). What it returns for an unknown name depends on regerror, which was not read.
note: contrib/netbsd-tests/lib/libc/regex/main.c:515-526 (slice 521-526 is the tail; the packet name regatoi does not exist in this directory: grep finds no definition or use; the slice contains efind).

name: ATF_TC_BODY(test04, tc)
prose: ATF test body for fmemopen in append modes. For each mode in "a", "ab", "a+", "ab+", "a+b" it fills a BUFSIZ buffer with the byte 0x01, opens it with fmemopen(buf, sizeof(buf), mode) and checks (ATF_CHECK, non-fatal; an assert when the standalone macros are used) that the stream is non-NULL and that buf[0] is still 0x01 (append mode does not truncate); on non-glibc systems it also checks that ftello(fp) equals sizeof(buf) (position at the end, because the buffer holds no NUL) and that after fseeko(fp, 0, SEEK_END) the position is again sizeof(buf); then it checks fclose(fp) == 0.
note: contrib/netbsd-tests/lib/libc/stdio/t_fmemopen.c:254-290 (the glibc checks are compiled out at :274-286).

name: ATF_TC_BODY(clearenv_basic, tc)
prose: ATF test body for a user clearing the environment directly. It sets 1024 variables crap0..crap1023 with setenv (each ATF_CHECK that the call does not return -1), then sets *environ = NULL (so the environment becomes empty without using clearenv), sets crap0 again, and checks that getenv("crap0") is "0" and that getenv("crap1") and getenv("crap2") are NULL. Checks are non-fatal.

name: ATF_TC_BODY(getenv_basic, tc)
prose: ATF test body for setenv/getenv/unsetenv. It sets EVIL to "very=bad" (ATF_CHECK success), checks getenv("EVIL") equals "very=bad", checks that getenv("EVIL=very") is NULL, and unsets EVIL, checking the call succeeds. Checks are non-fatal.

name: ATF_TC_BODY(putenv_basic, tc)
prose: ATF test body for putenv. It builds "crap=true" in a local array and calls putenv on it, checks getenv("crap") is "true", then changes string[1] to 'l' and checks getenv("clap") is "true" and getenv("crap") is NULL (the environment entry aliases the caller's array), restores string[1] to 'r', unsets crap and checks it is gone. It then checks that putenv(NULL), putenv("val") and putenv("=val") return -1 with errno EINVAL (ATF_CHECK_ERRNO). Checks are non-fatal.

name: ATF_TC_BODY(setenv_basic, tc)
prose: ATF test body (timeout 600 s) for setenv/getenv/unsetenv at scale. It picks a random offset and sets 8192 variables var0..var8191 in a permuted order to random values with overwrite 1, checks that setenv(name, "foo", 0) does not overwrite (getenv still returns the random value); then in another permuted order it unsets each variable, checks getenv returns NULL and that unsetting again succeeds. It then checks that setenv with a NULL name, an empty name and a name containing '=' return -1 with errno EINVAL; on FreeBSD it expects a SIGSEGV for the next check (setenv("var", NULL, 1) is not validated there); it checks setenv("var", NULL, 1) returns -1 with EINVAL, and that setenv("var", "=val", 1) returns 0 and getenv("var") is "=val". Checks are non-fatal.

name: ATF_TC_BODY(setenv_mixed, tc)
prose: ATF test body mixing setenv, putenv and unsetenv on one variable, mixedcrap. It copies "mixedcrap=putenv" into a local array; sets mixedcrap=setenv and checks getenv returns "setenv", calls putenv(string) and checks it returns "putenv", unsets it and checks it is NULL; then repeats in the other order (putenv, then setenv, then unsetenv) with the same checks. All checks are non-fatal.

name: ATF_TC_BODY(strtod_underflow, tc)
prose: ATF test body checking underflow detection in strtod. It parses a decimal string of the form 0.000...0002 with several hundred zeros after the point (a value far below the smallest double), after setting errno = 0, and calls atf_tc_fail (fatal) unless the result is exactly 0 and errno equals ERANGE.

name: ATF_TC_BODY(strtod_gherman_bug, tc)
prose: ATF test body for a strtod rounding bug reported by Geza Herman. It sets errno = 0, parses the string "1.8254370818746402660437411213933955878019332885742187" and checks with ATF_CHECK (non-fatal) that the result equals the hexadecimal double constant 0x1.d34fd8378ea83p+0 exactly.

name: ATF_TC_BODY(strtoi_signed, tc)
prose: ATF test body for signed parsing in strtoi(3), table-driven. For each entry of the table of fourteen cases (strings such as " -3", "--1", "+-2", "-1 3", "-1.3", "+33.", "30x0") it sets errno = 0, calls strtoi(str, &end, base 0, INTMAX_MIN, INTMAX_MAX, &e), calls atf_tc_fail if errno changed (note that the message prints e rather than errno), and calls check(), which uses atf_tc_fail_nonfatal to compare the returned value, the status code e (0, ECANCELED for a bad sign sequence, ENOTSUP for trailing garbage) and the end pointer with the table's expectations. Returns nothing.
note: contrib/netbsd-tests/lib/libc/stdlib/t_strtoi.c:244-293 (slice 277-304 holds the loop at :277-292; check() at :59-77). The packet name strtoi_table_test does not exist; this is the test body whose loop the slice contains.

name: ATF_TC_BODY(memccpy_simple, tc)
prose: ATF test body for memccpy. It fills a 100-byte buffer with ' ' and then checks (ATF_CHECK, non-fatal): memccpy(buf, "foo bar", ' ', 100) returns non-NULL (stops after copying the first blank, index 3) and buf[4] is still ' ' (the fill); memccpy(buf, "foo bar", '\0', 99) returns non-NULL (stops after the terminating NUL) and buf[8] is still ' '; memccpy(buf, "foo bar", 'x', 7) returns NULL (no 'x' in 7 bytes) and the first 7 bytes of buf equal "foo bar"; memccpy(buf, "xxxxxxx", 'r', 7) returns NULL (no 'r') and the first 7 bytes of buf now equal "xxxxxxx", i.e. buf is overwritten by the copy.
note: contrib/netbsd-tests/lib/libc/string/t_memcpy.c:121-139. Reviewer (r15) RIGHT: the last case changes buf to "xxxxxxx" (:137-138).

name: ATF_TC_BODY(fchroot_perm, tc)
prose: ATF test body (compiled only where the fchroot tests are enabled, i.e. NetBSD; requires root) checking that an unprivileged user cannot fchroot. It gets the current directory with getcwd (ATF_REQUIRE), looks up user "nobody" with getpwnam, opens the directory read-only (ATF_REQUIRE fd >= 0 and pw != NULL) and forks (ATF_REQUIRE). The child calls setuid(nobody) (result ignored), sets errno = 0 and calls fchroot(fd): it exits with EXIT_FAILURE if the call succeeded or if errno is not EPERM, and with EXIT_SUCCESS otherwise. The parent waits (result ignored) and calls atf_tc_fail unless the child exited normally with EXIT_SUCCESS. The descriptor is not closed. If setuid failed the child would still run with the original (root) credentials.

name: INVALID_UCONTEXT(amd64, pc_too_high, "instruction pointer outside userland address space")
prose: Helper generated by the INVALID_UCONTEXT macro for amd64: static void amd64_pc_too_high(ucontext_t *uc) sets the saved instruction pointer uc->uc_mcontext.__gregs[_REG_RIP] to VM_MAXUSER_ADDRESS, the first address above the user address space, and returns nothing. It is called by the generated test lwp_create_amd64_fail_pc_too_high, which does getcontext, sets uc_flags = _UC_CPU, applies the helper, and requires (fatal) that _lwp_create(&uc, 0, &lid) returns non-zero with errno EINVAL. Only compiled for __amd64__.

name: ATF_TC_CLEANUP(mkfifo_stat, tc)
prose: ATF cleanup routine for the mkfifo_stat test: calls unlink(path) on the relative path "fifo" and casts the result to void, so any error (for example the file not existing because the test already removed it, or a permission error) is ignored. Afterwards the path is gone only if it existed and unlink succeeded.
note: contrib/netbsd-tests/lib/libc/sys/t_mkfifo.c:261-264; path defined at :46. Reviewer (r15) RIGHT: the unlink result is ignored, so removal is not guaranteed.
